title: Teaching Task-Based Parallel Programming with a Runtime Systems-Aware Perspective
problem: Conventional explicit multithreading for multicore programming is complex; work organization and load balancing across threads difficult
motivation: Task-based models simplify parallel programming by abstracting thread management; teaching approach that grounds understanding in runtime systems implementation
method: Students implement a task-based parallel programming model (where work is broken into independent tasks and launched asynchronously with finish points to synchronize when they complete), then build a dynamic load-balancing runtime that distributes these tasks across processor cores. They iteratively improve both to handle real processor challenges like uneven task execution time and keeping data in fast cache memory.
key_novelty: The course teaches programming abstraction and runtime systems together—students implement both the task-based language construct and the runtime scheduler that makes it run efficiently, so they see how one depends on the other.
contributions: Structured curriculum for task-based parallel programming education
Qualitative and quantitative evaluation of course effectiveness
Demonstrated improved student understanding of parallel execution
limitations: Focus on education rather than novel hardware optimization; quantitative evaluation details limited in abstract
